transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-12
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Sam Torres (CTO - Mariner), Lena Kim (Head of Platform), Evan Chu (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Redwood walked Mariner through Redwood Optimize recommendations focused on batching and prefix/KV cache to reduce per-token cost while meeting 95th p latency SLOs.
- Discussed tradeoffs: larger batches vs latency, cache hit rates, memory & eviction policies, and model quantization impact.
- Agreed next steps: send pilot pricing, share security docs, schedule benchmark run with sample traffic.

Topics: batching strategy, prefix vs KV cache, cost model walkthrough, dedicated vs hosted routing, security and KMS, benchmark plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - we are on for 45 minutes, we'll run through Optimize, batching and KV- sorry K-V cache recommendations, cost model, and then leave time for Qs. Priya I'll hand to you for the deep bits.
[00:28] Priya: thanks Alex. hi Sam, Lena, Evan, nice to meet you. quick note, i'm Priya, i run inference performance at Redwood. we'll go through three things: batching basics, prefix vs kv cache, and a sample cost model for your payments workload.
[01:05] Sam: great, excited. our main goal is to get latency under 200ms p95 for customer-facing intents, but also keep cost predictable. right now we have a mix of short chat queries and longer form refunds flows.
[01:22] Priya: perfect, that mixed distribution is exactly where batching + KV caching can help. quick qual: what's your average sequence length on chat? and on refunds?
[01:40] Lena: chat is usually 20-40 tokens (model input), refunds flow can be 300-600 tokens depending on context. our traffic patterns peak at close of day and during promo events.
[02:02] Evan: also we have strict encryption needs, all logs must be offboarded to our KMS and audit retained for 12 months.
[02:18] Alex: noted - SOC2 and KMS are included in our enterprise pack, we'll attach docs. Priya?
[02:26] Priya: ok first, batching fundamentals: continuous batching in Redwood groups in-flight requests to amortize kernel launch & memory costs. imagine N requests merged into one forward pass - cost per token drops almost linearly with batch size up to hardware/seq limits.
[03:00] Priya: caveat - batching increases tail latency if you wait to fill large batches. so policy is pairing smart routing: short-latency paths for small requests, background batching for non-interactive work.
[03:28] Sam: can you do dynamic batching per-route? like our payments auth needs low latency, backfill tasks can be batched more.
[03:38] Priya: yes, per-route SLOs and batching profiles are first class - you can set a max queue time (eg 5-10ms) and a max batch size. Redwood's default tries to keep p95 within target while giving good throughput.
[04:05] Priya: next, prefix vs KV cache. prefix caching stores the model's past tokens (prefixes) at request time and reuses KV pairs for repeated prefixes, high value for structured flows like refund templates. KV cache refers to the transformer key/value cache for auto-regressive decoding; we persist and reuse it across requests when the prefix repeats.
[04:48] Evan: sorry i'm a bit fuzzy - prefix cache vs session cache? are these the same?
[04:53] Priya: good question - terminology is fuzzy. session cache is application-level; prefix cache here means we detect repeated prefixes (like same user prompt template) and reuse model KV state so decode cost is only for new tokens. it reduces decoder compute.
[05:15] Priya: practically, for Mariner, if refund flows start with the same 60-token system+prompt, we can cache that KV and only compute the variable tail. hit rates depend on how templated your prompts are.
[05:35] Sam: that would help a lot. our refunds do have templated intro + user fields substituted.
[05:44] Priya: OK next slide - cost model. we modeled three scenarios: no cache small batches, kv cache with small batches, and larger batch-heavy throughput. numbers are illustrative: baseline hosted gen cost = $X/token (we use normalized units in deck).
[06:10] Priya: sample: baseline per-req cost for 300-token refund ~ 300 units. with 60-token cached prefix hit rate 80%, decode only 240 tokens saved -> net 60 tokens computed, big saving. if hit rate drops to 30% savings smaller.
[06:46] Lena: are those units GPU milliseconds or money? we need $ estimates for budgeting.
[06:52] Priya: right - we'll map to dollars in the spreadsheet. e.g., on A100-class infra, unit->$0.000012/token approx in our conservative estimate. we'll include dedicated capacity pricing options too.
[07:20] Sam: what's the memory implication of persisting KV for many sessions? we have 100k concurrent sessions at times.
[07:30] Priya: good callout. KV memory scales with seq_len * hidden_size * 2 (keys+values), so we recommend TTL-based eviction, LRU and size caps. for large concurrency, we only persist for high-value flows or use prefix digests to avoid full KV storage.
[07:55] Evan: so we wouldn't cache everything by default. is there tooling to measure hit-rate per prompt?
[08:02] Priya: yes, Optimize console shows per-prompt hit rate, top templates, and suggested cache candidate prefixes. it also simulates cost impact if you enable caching for certain templates.
[08:20] Alex: quick product note - we also show recommended batching settings per-route based on observed seq distribution; you can accept suggestions or tune.
[08:35] Sam: how does this work with dedicated vs hosted? we prefer a dedicated pool for PCI compliance but not sure about scale.
[08:45] Priya: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity, so batching behavior is more predictable, and KV caching memory is local to your pool. Hosted is multi-tenant but we provide VPC peering and encrypted links. For PCI we often recommend Dedicated or Private deployment.
[09:10] Lena: private deployment allowed for on-prem? we have some regs that may require that.
[09:15] Alex: yes, Redwood Private is available - we can discuss network diagrams and KMS/HSM integration in the security pack we send.
[09:29] Priya: back to tradeoffs: bigger batches -> lower $/token but higher p95. KV cache -> reduces decode cost but increases memory footprint and complexity. combined they usually give best wins if you have templated prefixes.
[09:55] Priya: example chart: at 60% cache hit and batch size 16, cost per 1k requests down by ~45% vs baseline. if hit=20% benefit drops to ~18%.
[10:18] Sam: what's the recommended batch size for our refund 300-600 token flows?
[10:24] Priya: for long sequences, batch sizes of 4-8 often hit sweet spot on latency; for short chat (20-40 tokens) you can push 16-32 if you accept slightly higher tail latency. but rule of thumb is per-route tuning.
[10:49] Evan: On the implementation side, what does app dev have to change? do we have to manage prefix ids?
[10:56] Priya: minimal changes: tag templated prompts with a prefix key (we can auto-detect many templates), pass an optional cache_key in API. Redwood handles KV lookup and fallback. we also provide SDK helpers.
[11:18] Alex: i'll put that in the follow-up doc.
[11:24] Priya: now demo - i'll share the console view. (screen share noise)
[11:40] Priya: here's Optimize's suggestions tab - you can see routes, avg seq, suggested batch, suggested max_queue_ms, and candidate prefixes with estimated hit rates. this is from a synthetic workload - numbers are approximate.
[12:10] Lena: that UI where it recommends prefixes - is it safe to auto-enable? concerns about PII cached.
[12:18] Priya: very important - we allow opt-out and scrubbing rules. by default we don't cache PII; you can set pattern rules or only cache system-level prefixes. plus customer-owned KMS for persisted cache payloads.
[12:38] Sam: good. on scrubbing, can we hash user-specific fields before indexing for cache keys?
[12:44] Priya: yes that's common - normalize and hash PII, create stable prefix digest. Redwood has helper functions in SDK.
[12:59] Evan: what's the eviction policy in practice? LRU or TTL?
[13:04] Priya: both - TTL default 24h for ephemeral, LRU on memory pressure. you can tune per-route.
[13:20] Priya: moving to the cost spreadsheet briefly - (reads numbers) for 1M requests/mo with 30% long refund flows, enabling KV for refund templates cuts infra tokens by ~25% equating to $2.1k/mo savings on our model; with dedicated and reserved discounts it improves further.
[13:50] Sam: can we see the spreadsheet?
[13:53] Alex: i'll attach when we send follow-up. Priya can compile a mariner-tailored sheet.
[14:00] Priya: sure - i'll generate two sheets: hosted price mapping and dedicated commit mapping.
[14:12] Sam: two more security Qs: SSO for console and audit logs forwarding?
[14:18] Alex: yes SAML SSO/SCIM provisioning supported; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM, encrypted at rest, with 12-month retention per enterprise pack.
[14:34] Lena: KMS integration - bring-your-own-key?
[14:38] Priya: BYOK supported, HSM tie-ins for Private deployments too. we'll include KMS diagram in the packet.
[14:50] Evan: latency wise, does KV caching add an extra network hop? like if we persist KV in a separate store?
[14:58] Priya: our design keeps KV near the runtime; for Dedicated it's local GPU memory or a fast in-host cache. network overhead is minimal compared to decoding cost; if you externalize KV store there would be extra latency, which is why we prefer local.
[15:20] Sam: what about cold-starts for new prefixes?
[15:24] Priya: cold-starts pay full decode cost until prefix is cached; we often recommend warmup runs for heavy campaigns or pre-caching during low-traffic windows.
[15:38] Alex: let's open floor for technical questions.
[15:44] Sam: on batching again - how deterministic is p95 under peak? will queueing cause spikes?
[15:52] Priya: with per-route max_queue_ms set, you cap added queue latency. Redwood runtime also supports burst capacity to reduce queuing on transient spikes. dedicated lets you size to avoid persistent queuing.
[16:14] Evan: is there telemetry we can export to our observability? we want token-level traces correlated with request IDs.
[16:20] Priya: yes, trace hooks and per-token cost breakdown available. we send logs to your endpoint or to S3.
[16:34] Lena: curious about multi-model fallbacks you mentioned earlier - if a big model is unavailable, you fallback to a quantized variant? how are outputs compared?
[16:44] Priya: fallback policy allows model variants; we include a quality delta estimate from our eval harness. you can configure automatic degrade only if quality delta < threshold.
[17:03] Sam: earlier you mentioned quantization recommendations. will that affect accuracy for refund classification?
[17:10] Priya: quantization (4-bit/8-bit) often has minimal impact for many tasks, but we recommend running a small eval set - Optimize can run such tests to measure regressions. (laugh) that's my favorite feature.
[17:32] Evan: can Optimize run the eval against our labeled sets?
[17:36] Priya: yes, with an upload of a small eval set (we have privacy modes), it can run regression tests and produce an ROC/accuracy delta table.
[17:50] Sam: what's typical timeline for a pilot?
[17:54] Alex: commonly 4-8 weeks: week 1-2 config and security review, week 2-4 run benchmarks and tune, week 5-8 finalize SLA/commits.
[18:07] Lena: budget wise, can you give a sample committed capacity pricing?
[18:12] Alex: we'll include tiered pricing in the follow-up. sample: monthly reserved GPU pool + per-token for overflow.
[18:22] Priya: quick demo snippet - here's simulated traffic in the console. you can toggle candidate prefixes and preview cache hit simulation. (small pause)
[18:48] Alex: a note on instrumentation: to get best results, attach user_id or session_id and mark template keys; Optimize's analysis improves with more data.
[19:02] Sam: we can do that. we'll need dev time to tag templates; how much effort?
[19:09] Priya: minimal - usually a couple engineers a day to tag and integrate SDK calls for cache_key. we can provide a checklist.
[19:23] Evan: For eviction, if we persist many prefixes, do we charge extra for memory? how is that priced?
[19:30] Priya: memory for KV is included in dedicated pricing tiers up to a cap; extra memory beyond that can be negotiated or you can enable per-prefix TTL. we'll show numbers in the cost sheet.
[19:47] Sam: any compliance issues with caching? we must ensure PII isn't stored.
[19:52] Priya: default is to avoid caching PII; also you can set scrubbing rules or hash PII as discussed. for Private deployment you can keep all cache on-prem.
[20:08] Lena: ok can you walk the cost model numbers one more time slowly?
[20:12] Priya: sure. baseline scenario: no cache, batch size 4, avg token cost X. scenario two: enable prefix KV for templated refunds with 60% hit, keep batch 8 for background, net token compute reduces by Y%, converting to $ gives $ savings. scenario three: dedicated reserved gives discount Z%.
[20:46] Alex: (interrupt) i'll summarize in the email.
[20:50] Sam: If we enable KV cache, what about model updates? if we roll model version, do cached KVs remain valid?
[20:59] Priya: good question - typically KV caches are variant-specific. when you change model or big tokenizer changes, you should invalidate relevant cache keys; Redwood supports rolling invalidations at prefix level.
[21:20] Evan: any support for multi-tenant cache partitioning? we need isolation between tenants.
[21:26] Priya: yes per-tenant namespaces and RBAC on cache controls.
[21:38] Lena: i want to ensure we can audit who sees cache keys. is there per-action logging?
[21:44] Alex: yes audit logs include actions on caches, who changed TTLs, who enabled prefixes.
[21:55] Sam: are we able to run a benchmark with our sample traffic in a staging dedicated pool?
[22:01] Alex: absolutely - that's one of the next steps. we'll provision a staging pool and run a 24-72h benchmark.
[22:11] Priya: can you share sample traffic and a SRE contact for onboarding?
[22:16] Sam: Evan will take that.
[22:18] Evan: yep, i'll share by EOD Monday.
[22:22] Priya: great. quick Q: do you have latency SLOs for each route?
[22:27] Sam: target for auth and customer-facing intents is 200ms p95, background analytics can be > 1s.
[22:36] Priya: noted - we'll propose batching/queue settings to meet that.
[22:43] Alex: let's go through a short hypothetical: refund flow is templated 60-token prefix plus 200 token variable. with 80% prefix hit and batch size 6 we hit 150ms p95 in our sim.
[23:02] Sam: optimistic, good.
[23:06] Priya: caveat: those sims assume dedicated GPUs and warm cache.
[23:13] Evan: warm cache - does Redwood provide pre-warm APIs?
[23:18] Priya: yes we can pre-cache prefixes via admin API or run synthetic warmers.
[23:30] Lena: any gotchas for model safety? we need to ensure deterministic outputs for certain regulatory transcripts.
[23:36] Priya: caching does not change decoding algorithm; if you care about determinism, we'll note seed/temperature and run control tests during eval.
[23:51] Alex: ok we are approaching Q&A - want to collect any remaining concerns.
[23:58] Sam: timeline and price are main. also show us end-to-end how we'd integrate with our SSO and KMS.
[24:07] Alex: we'll include a sample integration plan and timeline in follow-up.
[24:13] Evan: one last technical: when you say "KV cache persisted to disk" - is that actually persisted to disk or just memory?
[24:21] Priya: typically kept in memory for speed; optional disk-backed snapshots for failover. disk snapshots are not used on hot path.
[24:36] Lena: curious about maintenance windows and patching for dedicated pools.
[24:41] Alex: Dedicated has scheduled maintenance windows and options for canary patching; Private you control maintenance.
[24:50] Priya: i'll jump into recommended config checklist: 1) identify templated prompts and tag prefix keys, 2) set per-route max_queue_ms and max_batch, 3) enable KV for selected templates, 4) set TTL and eviction, 5) run 72h benchmark and iterate.
[25:20] Priya: example configs for Mariner: route auth-chat -> max_queue_ms 10ms, max_batch 8; refunds-route -> max_queue_ms 20ms, max_batch 6, KV enabled for prefixes with hit>40%.
[25:44] Sam: that seems reasonable.
[25:48] Alex: we'll send these as part of the pilot onboarding doc.
[25:55] Priya: security reminder: for any cached prefixes that may contain PII, set scrubbing rules or don't cache. also you can pass a flag to store only in customer-managed KMS.
[26:12] Evan: dev ops question: how is cache invalidation API authenticated?
[26:18] Alex: via RBAC tokens and audit logged; we can demo token creation in the next session.
[26:30] Lena: are there any examples of banks using Redwood caching?
[26:36] Priya: yes - Aurora Finance and Novapay have similar setups; we can share anonymized case studies.
[26:51] Sam: sweet. credits question - any free trial for this pilot?
[26:56] Alex: we often offer limited credits and a discounted reserved tier for pilot customers; details in proposal.
[27:06] Priya: last technical note: if you have very long prefix lengths, sometimes compressing the prefix (token pipelining) helps reduce KV size; Optimize recommends transform steps.
[27:24] Evan: interesting.
[27:28] Sam: OK wrap up?
[27:31] Alex: sure - recap: Alex will send pricing/proposal + security pack; Priya will prepare a tailored cost model and sample config; Evan will share sample traffic. target benchmark week of Apr 26.
[27:50] Lena: timeline works. please include contact points for SRE and security.
[27:55] Alex: will do.
[28:00] (brief off-topic chatter / people leaving)
[28:20] Priya: any final questions?
[28:25] Sam: none from me, thanks.
[28:28] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[28:33] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings present ("K-V cash" etc). timestamps approximate.
